OpenAI just gutted its safety team — the people whose entire job is to make sure AI doesn't go catastrophically wrong.

But it gets worse. The people you fire don't disappear. They go to Anthropic, DeepMind, or start their own labs. You just redistributed your safety talent directly to competitors.

What this signals is a clear priority shift. Speed over safety. Ship it now, figure out consequences later. That's the bet OpenAI is making.

And if that bet is wrong — even once — the consequences aren't a bad product launch. They're something nobody has a playbook for.
